text: Here is a mistake the examiners list for exactly this word, on the card. The question asked for the term that describes an enzyme which is secreted and catalyzes reactions outside cells. Read this answer. Look at the prefix. It starts with ex, it ends with cellular, and it feels right, because ex means out and the enzyme is out of the cell. One reason this can feel right is that they have just learnt that the enzyme leaves the cell, and the word for leaving blurs into the word for where it works. But the examiners' list of common mistakes shows four different ex words offered, and the term credited is extracellular: the syllabus's own word, and the one credited in November 2020 when you had to underline the terms that describe lipases. So write it in full, extracellular enzyme. And catalyst on its own was not credited either: it says what the enzyme does, not where.
